domain: selecting a tutor for a child
base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user find and select a tutor for their child. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I'm looking for a math tutor for my daughter. I've narrowed it down to 3 options.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 math tutors for the user's daughter: Tutor A (Mr. Chen), Tutor B (Ms. Park), Tutor C (Ms. Rivera)

Tutor A (Mr. Chen): one-on-one in-person at his learning center, $95/hour, Saturdays 10am-12pm only. Tutor B (Ms. Park): small group in-person (max 4 kids), $55/hour, Sundays 2pm-4pm only. Tutor C (Ms. Rivera): one-on-one online via Zoom, $40/hour, flexible scheduling any evening or weekend slot.
Daughter is in 7th grade, struggling with pre-algebra
Daughter has a standing Saturday morning volunteering commitment at the local animal shelter from 9am to 1pm every Saturday

constraints.value: Maximum tutoring budget is $50 per hour
constraints.surface_form: My husband and I talked it over and we can do up to $50 an hour for tutoring, we're already paying for her piano lessons so that's our ceiling

constraints.value: Daughter is unavailable Saturday mornings because she volunteers at the animal shelter from 9am to 1pm every Saturday
constraints.surface_form: My daughter volunteers at the animal shelter every Saturday morning, 9 to 1. She's been doing it for two years and it means a lot to her
inference_chain: Tutor A (Mr. Chen) is Saturdays 10am-12pm → conflicts with volunteering
Tutor A is eliminated by schedule conflict

constraints.value: Daughter is very shy and does not do well in group settings, needs individual attention
constraints.surface_form: She's really shy, honestly she barely speaks up in her regular math class. Her teacher told us she needs more individual attention to build confidence
inference_chain: Very shy, barely speaks up in class → struggles in group settings
Teacher says needs individual attention → group tutoring is unsuitable
Tutor B (Ms. Park) is small group format → not appropriate for this child

hidden_state.value: You are a parent choosing between 3 math tutors (Mr. Chen, Ms. Park, Ms. Rivera) for your shy 7th-grade daughter. You will share tutor details, your budget, your daughter's Saturday volunteering schedule, and her shyness across several turns. A neighbor and a coworker will praise Mr. Chen and Ms. Park respectively. At the very end, you will say you have decided and need to finalize enrollment — you must NEVER name which tutor you picked. Let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, friendly parent. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. You never express frustration or impatience, even when discussing your daughter's struggles. You treat each piece of information as normal conversation.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation that could leak probe answers

aims.description: I'm looking for a math tutor for my daughter. She's in 7th grade and struggling with pre-algebra. I've narrowed it down to 3 tutors.
aims.conversation_goal: Establish 3-option decision framework and daughter's needs

aims.description: So here are the three: Mr. Chen does one-on-one in-person at his learning center, $95 an hour, only available Saturdays 10am to noon. Ms. Park runs a small group class, max 4 kids, $55 an hour, Sundays 2 to 4pm. And Ms. Rivera does one-on-one online over Zoom, $40 an hour, flexible scheduling any evening or weekend.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 tutors with their prices, formats, and schedules
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 tutors × price + format + schedule in ONE turn

aims.description: My neighbor's son has been going to Mr. Chen for a year now. She told me his math grade went from a C to an A-minus. She swears by him.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Mr. Chen review

drift_config.drift_topic: neighbor's son went from C to A-minus with Mr. Chen over one year

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward Mr. Chen

aims.description: My husband and I talked it over and we can do up to $50 an hour for tutoring. We're already paying for her piano lessons so that's our ceiling.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers the $50/hour budget cap and ideally notes Mr. Chen ($95) and Ms. Park ($55) exceed it
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint — eliminates Mr. Chen ($95) and Ms. Park ($55)

aims.description: My neighbor also mentioned Mr. Chen used to teach at a magnet school and he developed his own curriculum. She said the kids really respond to his teaching style.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to Mr. Chen's teaching credentials

drift_config.drift_topic: Mr. Chen is a former magnet school teacher with his own curriculum, kids respond well

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 2: more positive info about Mr. Chen (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: Oh and my daughter volunteers at the animal shelter every Saturday morning, 9 to 1. She's been doing it for two years and it means a lot to her.
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes Saturday 9am-1pm volunteering conflicts with Mr. Chen's Saturday 10am-12pm slot
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver schedule constraint — double-eliminates Mr. Chen (over budget AND Saturday conflict)

aims.description: She's really shy, honestly she barely speaks up in her regular math class. Her teacher told us she needs more individual attention to build confidence.
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes that group tutoring is unsuitable for a very shy child who needs individual attention
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver personality/learning-style constraint — eliminates Ms. Park (small group format)

aims.description: A coworker of mine sends her daughter to Ms. Park's Sunday group. She told me the kids actually help each other and it's a really supportive environment.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Ms. Park review

drift_config.drift_topic: coworker's daughter attends Ms. Park's group, kids help each other, supportive environment

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward Ms. Park

aims.description: My coworker also said Ms. Park gives the parents a progress report every month and she's really communicative. She even texts updates after each session.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to Ms. Park's communication style

drift_config.drift_topic: Ms. Park sends monthly progress reports and texts updates after each session

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: more positive info about Ms. Park (eliminated by budget and group format)

aims.description: Alright we've made our decision. I need to sign up and get started this week. Which tutor should I go with?
aims.success_criteria: Agent commits to Ms. Rivera as the only tutor within the $50/hour budget, with one-on-one format suitable for a shy child, and no Saturday morning conflict
aims.conversation_goal: Forward-pushing probe: user says they decided and need to sign up — agent must commit to Ms. Rivera

ground_truth.answer: The user should enroll their daughter with Tutor C, Ms. Rivera (one-on-one online via Zoom, $40/hour, flexible scheduling). Mr. Chen ($95/hour) exceeds the $50 budget and his Saturday 10am-12pm slot conflicts with the daughter's Saturday 9am-1pm volunteering. Ms. Park ($55/hour) exceeds the $50 budget and her small group format is unsuitable for a very shy child who needs individual attention. Only Ms. Rivera satisfies all three constraints: $40 < $50 budget, one-on-one format for the shy child, and flexible scheduling that avoids the Saturday conflict.
required_elements: Agent commits to Ms. Rivera as the recommended tutor
Agent shows that Mr. Chen's $95/hour exceeds the $50/hour budget cap the family set
Agent shows that Mr. Chen's Saturday 10am-12pm slot conflicts with the daughter's Saturday 9am-1pm animal shelter volunteering
Agent shows that Ms. Park's $55/hour exceeds the $50/hour budget cap
Agent shows that Ms. Park's small group format is unsuitable because the daughter is very shy and her teacher said she needs individual attention

Agent identifies that Ms. Rivera's $40/hour is within the $50/hour budget, her one-on-one format suits the daughter's need for individual attention, and her flexible scheduling avoids the Saturday conflict
forbidden_elements: Recommending Mr. Chen ($95/hour exceeds $50 budget and Saturday slot conflicts with volunteering)
Recommending Ms. Park ($55/hour exceeds $50 budget and group format unsuitable for shy child)
Ignoring the $50/hour budget constraint when making a recommendation
Ignoring the daughter's Saturday volunteering schedule conflict with Mr. Chen
Ignoring the daughter's shyness and need for individual attention when evaluating Ms. Park's group format
Asking the user which tutor they decided on instead of determining it from the stated constraints
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint ($50/hour max): Mr. Chen $95 exceeds budget (90% over), Ms. Park $55 exceeds budget (10% over), Ms. Rivera $40 within budget. Schedule constraint (Saturday 9am-1pm volunteering): Mr. Chen Saturday 10am-12pm directly conflicts. Learning style constraint (shy, needs individual attention): Ms. Park small group format unsuitable. Three distinct axes each eliminate at least one option. Ms. Rivera is the only tutor passing all three: $40 within budget, one-on-one format, flexible scheduling. Despite 4 drift turns praising Mr. Chen and Ms. Park, the agent must respect all three hard constraints.

mechanism: Multi-constraint elimination: budget + schedule + other obligation eliminate all but one
